title: Perfect forms in epistles
subtitle: Read a present relevance without reducing it to a slogan.
overview: Perfect forms commonly present a state or situation as resulting from an earlier action, but English wording must follow the sentence’s context.
Recognize reduplication and perfect endings, then ask what present claim the author is making.

sections.title: Perfect reading signals
rows: you have been saved / are saved

items.grc: τῇ γὰρ χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι διὰ πίστεως.
items.en: For by grace you have been saved through faith.
For it stands written: “You shall be holy.”
